source.commit_body:
Earnings AMC fix:
  EarningsDate.call_time was previously ignored. find_spanning_earnings
  treated 'announcement_date' as the day price reaction appears, but for
  AMC events (call_time >= 16:00 ET, ~7,729 of 16,420 events in DB),
  the gap actually shows up on the NEXT trading day. Trades entered AT
  THE CLOSE of the announcement day were incorrectly classified as
  non-spanning, so vega ratio was never sampled and the option-pricing
  model under-counted IV crush. MDLZ Apr 28 -> Apr 29 case is the
  poster child: earnings was Apr 28 AMC, reaction Apr 29, but
  find_spanning_earnings(entry=Apr-28, exit=Apr-29) returned None
  because the strict 'entry < ed <= exit' check needs Apr 28 < Apr 28.

  New helper iv_crush_model.compute_effective_date(date, call_time,
  trading_days=None) returns:
    BMO/intraday: announcement_date
    AMC: next trading day (uses calendar if provided, else weekday fallback)

  Applied at all earnings-loading sites:
    - database/models/core.py: 3 sites (live + 2 batched paths) now use
      _load_effective_earnings_dates(symbol) for EARN_BOOST proximity AND
      volume-amplifier earnings-window detection (earnings_set)
    - monte_carlo.py: ern_map_for_iv (always loaded now, no longer gated
      by IV_CRUSH_ENABLED), _earnings_suppress_filter (EARN_SUPP_PUT),
      EARN_BOOST_CALL ern_by_sym
    - backtest_cascade.py: _earnings_suppress_puts ed_map

  This is a SCORE-STAGE change (EARN_BOOST proximity + volume amplifier
  earnings_dates_set both consume effective_dates) — recalculate required.

Realized-fill sampling refactor [low,high] (replaces [open,close]):
  resolve(outcome, rng) now samples U_fire uniform across the bar's full
  intraday range [low, high] instead of [open, close]. Two benefits:
    1. Honestly captures the full bar's path uncertainty
    2. Eliminates the 50/50 coin flip on 'both barriers breached' cases —
       the sample naturally lands on TP-side, SL-side, or in-between
       weighted by how much of the bar's range sits on each side
  Backtest_cascade.py mid-fill switched to (high+low)/2 (deterministic
  equivalent of uniform mid). Slippage now applied based on realized P&L
  sign (favorable -> SLIP_TP, adverse -> SLIP_SL).
